page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.large is a memory-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs from 1 physical core with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a baseline frequency of 2.5 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 8.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.r5.large in the lower tiers for compute and memory throughput. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved a single-core CPU score of 1099.88 and a multi-core score of 1461.58. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 81.48 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 10.42 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 981.0 and a multi-core score of 1184.0. Database performance via Redis SET operations reached 1.44 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput was measured at 1.75 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its low processing and memory speed relative to its high memory capacity. While it provides a high resource density of 8.0 GB RAM per core, the underlying Intel Xeon 8163 hardware delivers lower processing throughput per vCPU. This makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU calculations. Appropriate workloads include small-scale caching layers, lightweight database operations, basic web serving, and memory-intensive utility tasks that can tolerate lower CPU performance.
